title: Trie with top-k autocomplete
summary: Build a prefix tree that accumulates query weights and returns the k most popular completions of any prefix.

complexity.time: O(p + n + m log k), p = prefix length, n = nodes below it, m = words below it

hints: Every word that starts with a prefix lives in the subtree under the node you reach by walking the prefix one character at a time. Walk there first; if a character is missing, there are no completions.

Each node needs a map from character to child and a weight that is 0 unless a word ends there. Re-inserting a word adds to that weight instead of replacing it, so the weight counts how often the query was seen.

From the prefix node, do a depth-first walk that carries the characters spelled so far and collects (word, weight) wherever weight > 0. Then rank by weight descending and word ascending (sort, or a heap of size k) and keep the first k.
